This steering is usually provided by the rider, but under certain conditions, may be provided by the bicycle itself. The combined center of mass of a bicycle and its rider must lean into a turn. This lean is induced by a method known as countersteering, which can be performed by the rider turning the handlebars directly with the hands or indirectly by leaning the bicycle. The bicycle is extraordinarily efficient in both biological and mechanical terms.
